setups: Three of them come out of the chicken shop doorway like they've been stood in there a while. Because they have.
You're at the cashpoint. You hear a moped slow down behind you and you already know how this goes.
Bloke walks straight at you, no swerve, no eye contact. That's not how people walk unless it's deliberate.
Two others and a face you half-know. He's got that look people get when they've been told something about you.
The lift stops on the fourth floor. You didn't press four.
They're waiting by your block. Not hiding. Waiting. Which is worse.
Car pulls up alongside at walking pace and stays there for eleven seconds. You count them.
Two lads, one of them can't be more than eighteen, and he's the one holding it, and that's the problem.
You come out of Bossman's and the street's emptied. Streets don't empty for nothing.
Someone says your name. Nobody good has ever said your name like that.
